overview: BlueScope Steel is a global, vertically diversified steel manufacturer headquartered in Australia, best known for its COLORBOND, ZINCALUME and TRUECORE branded coated and painted steel products for building and construction. The Group operates an integrated steelworks at Port Kembla (NSW) plus a lower-cost electric-arc-furnace mini-mill (North Star BlueScope) in Ohio, alongside downstream buildings/coated-products businesses in North America, a steel mill and long-products business in New Zealand, and capital-light coating/painting joint ventures across Southeast Asia and China. It reports five segments: Australian Steel Products (ASP), North Star, Buildings and Coated Products North America (BCPNA), Coated Products Asia (CPA), and New Zealand & Pacific Islands (NZPI), with FY2026 group sales revenue of A$16.6 billion.

business_model.summary: BlueScope makes money by converting iron ore/scrap and other raw materials into flat and long steel products, then coating and painting a large share of that steel into higher-margin, branded building products. Earnings are highly cyclical, driven by regional steel 'spreads' (selling price less input costs, chiefly iron ore, coking coal, scrap and energy) rather than by steady, recurring revenue; North Star in the US is a low-cost electric-arc-furnace mini-mill that has become the largest single profit driver. Customers are almost entirely B2B/wholesale: builders, fabricators, distributors, OEMs and construction companies, with no meaningful direct consumer revenue despite strong end-consumer brand recognition (COLORBOND).

revenue_streams.name: Buildings and Coated Products North America (BCPNA)
Coated Products Asia (Thailand, Indonesia, Vietnam, Malaysia, China JV)

business_model.customer_type: B2B - builders, fabricators, distributors, manufacturers, OEMs; no material direct-to-consumer sales
business_model.geographic_mix: Australia ~41% of segment revenue, North America ~46% (North Star + BCPNA), Asia ~11%, New Zealand & Pacific ~5% (FY2026 segment revenue basis)

main_competitors: Nippon Steel (JV partner in NS BlueScope Coated Products and Asian JVs)
competitive_position.market_position: Largest steel manufacturer in Australia and sole steel producer in New Zealand; COLORBOND holds an estimated ~90% share of the Australian metal-roofing segment. North Star is one of the lowest-cost, highest-utilisation hot-rolled-coil mills in North America. A mid-sized global player overall, well behind Chinese, Indian and major US integrated/EAF producers by tonnage, but differentiated by its branded, value-added downstream franchise.

moat_factors.description: COLORBOND, ZINCALUME, TRUECORE and LYSAGHT are entrenched, trusted brands in Australian/NZ building and construction, commanding price premiums and channel loyalty that commodity steel producers cannot easily replicate

Modern electric-arc-furnace mini-mill located near scrap supply and customers in the US Midwest gives North Star industry-leading utilisation and margin performance, and it is currently running at full post-expansion capacity

Section 232 US tariffs (raised to 50% in 2025) and Australian/NZ anti-dumping measures currently support domestic pricing for North Star and BCP, though this is a policy-dependent advantage rather than a structural one
Local manufacturing footprint close to customers in each geography reduces supply-chain risk, shipping costs and margin volatility versus pure importers

Owns midstream (steelmaking) through downstream (coating, painting, building systems) capability, capturing more value-add than a pure commodity mill, and increasingly capital-light growth in Asia via JV coating/painting lines

weaknesses: Fundamentally a cyclical commodity manufacturer with limited pricing power outside its branded niches; earnings swing enormously with global steel spreads
Heavily exposed to Chinese steel overcapacity/export dumping, which structurally depresses Asian benchmark spreads and pressures BlueScope's Australian export and Asian businesses
BlueScope Coated Products (BCP) in North America has underperformed since acquisition, resulting in a $438.9 million impairment in FY2025; execution risk remains on the turnaround
Capital intensity is high (major projects such as the 6BF reline at ~$1.3bn, MCL7 at ~$490m, NZ EAF at ~NZ$320m), tying up capital for multi-year periods with execution risk
New Zealand & Pacific Islands segment has been loss-making/marginal for several years and is mid-transition to a new operating model

growth_drivers: North Star debottlenecking targeting ~300ktpa of additional low-cost steelmaking capacity, plus continued high-utilisation running at record production levels
Group target of ~$500 million of additional annual EBIT by 2030 from projects already underway (>$200m North America, >$125m Australia, ~$75m Asia, ~$75m New Zealand)
Port Kembla No.6 Blast Furnace reline and plate mill upgrade shifting export tonnes into higher-margin domestic/value-added sales
Western Sydney Metal Coating Line 7 (MCL7) adding 240ktpa of premium COLORBOND/TRUECORE capacity, now ramping up
New Zealand hybrid Electric Arc Furnace lowering NZ Steel's cost base and emissions intensity, supported by NZ government co-funding
$200m FY2026 cost/productivity program fully delivered, with a further ~$150m net cost benefit targeted for FY2027 from the operating model reset
Accelerating monetisation of BlueScope's ~1,200-hectare surplus industrial land portfolio (e.g., West Dapto land sale, Western Port logistics hub)
Capital-light, high-ROIC growth in Southeast Asian coating/painting JVs as regional construction markets mature
Increasing shareholder distributions (target of at least 75% of free cash flow) via ordinary dividends, special dividends and buybacks as major capex programs complete

business.description: Earnings are highly sensitive to regional steel spreads (selling price less iron ore, coking coal, scrap, energy costs); the FY2022 upcycle peak (~A$2.2bn underlying EBIT) versus FY2025 trough (~A$738m) illustrates the swing
Sustained Chinese oversupply keeps Asian benchmark spreads structurally depressed, weighing on ASP export sales and CPA/China performance
Aluminium, concrete, composites, plastic and timber compete with steel in various end-use applications and could erode volumes if relative economics or embodied-carbon perceptions shift
BCP suffered a $438.9m impairment in FY2025 on integration/performance issues; while FY2026 showed improvement, the turnaround is not complete
Large capital projects (6BF reline ~$1.3bn, MCL7 ~$490m, NZ EAF ~NZ$320m) carry cost-overrun and schedule risk during construction/ramp-up phases

financial.risk: Net debt increase and reduced balance sheet headroom
financial.description: Net debt rose from $28.4m to $600.0m in FY2026 (gearing 0.3% to 5.2%) as shareholder distributions were funded ahead of the completion of major capex; still within BlueScope's stated $1.5bn target ceiling

A stronger A$:US$ reduced FY2026 net assets by ~$385m via translation and created a $60m unfavourable EBIT translation impact; large US and Asian earnings bases mean FX volatility materially affects reported AUD results

Recent large special dividends (170cps FY2026) and target of $3.00/share in CY2027 are underwritten by currently elevated US spreads; a spread reversal would pressure the ability to sustain this distribution level

regulatory.description: North Star's outsized FY2026 earnings improvement was driven substantially by the doubling of Section 232 tariffs to 50% in 2025; any reduction, carve-out, or trade-deal rollback of these tariffs would materially compress North Star spreads and group earnings

Changes to tariffs, anti-dumping duties or local-content rules in any operating jurisdiction can directly affect BlueScope's sales volumes, pricing and competitiveness, as already seen in shifting export mix away from North America

Emerging carbon pricing, emissions regulation and potential carbon border measures could raise costs of iron/steelmaking; BlueScope is pursuing NeoSmelt and EAF pathways but commercially viable low-emissions steelmaking at scale remains unproven
The Board disclosed it rejected unsolicited acquisition proposals during FY2026 that it considered undervalued the company, creating periodic corporate-activity uncertainty

macro.risk: Global construction and industrial cycle sensitivity
macro.description: Demand is tied to residential/non-residential construction, automotive, manufacturing and infrastructure activity across Australia, the US, NZ and Asia — all sensitive to interest rates and broader economic growth

Iron ore, coking coal, scrap steel and energy price swings can compress margins if not passed through to steel prices, and rapid price movements create inventory valuation and working-capital volatility

macro.risk: Interest rate sensitivity via construction demand and cost of debt
macro.description: Higher rates depress residential/non-residential construction activity (a key demand driver) while also raising BlueScope's own funding costs as net debt increases

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Global steel industry outlook is bifurcated: US markets remain supported by Section 232 tariffs and firm mini-mill utilisation, Australian conditions are recovering with housing and data-centre-driven non-residential demand, and Southeast Asian markets show solid momentum, while China and broader Asian benchmark spreads stay structurally weak on persistent overcapacity and export intensity.
macro_factors.cyclicality: High - BlueScope is a classic late-cycle industrial/commodity business; underlying EBIT ranged from roughly $738m (FY2025 trough) to over $2.2bn (FY2022 peak) within a few years
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate - primarily indirect through construction and industrial demand (residential/non-residential approvals, infrastructure spend) and directly through rising net debt/finance costs as capex and distributions increase

recent_developments.event: FY2026 results: sales revenue $16,605.9M (+2%), underlying EBIT $1,273.4M (+73% YoY) driven by higher US steel spreads, reported NPAT $802.0M (+857% YoY, against a low FY2025 base that included the BCP impairment)

Board declared FY2026 final unfranked dividend of 65.0cps plus an unfranked special dividend of 70.0cps, completing a planned $3.00/share of CY2026 shareholder returns; confirmed intention to deliver a further $3.00/share in CY2027
1H FY2027 underlying EBIT guidance of $860M-$960M, supported by materially higher US mini-mill benchmark spreads (~US$750/t) and improving Asian spreads
1H FY2026 results: underlying EBIT $557.5M (+81% YoY) on stronger US steel spreads, higher volumes, lower costs and favourable FX; net debt fell to $2.2M

Tania Archibald commenced as Managing Director and CEO, succeeding Mark Vassella who retired after eight years in the role and 30 years with the company; board renewal also continued with new non-executive director appointments

Completed sale of BlueScope's 50% interest in the Tata BlueScope Steel (TBSL) India joint venture to partner Tata Steel, simplifying the Asian footprint and generating a non-assessable gain that lowered the FY2026 effective tax rate

US Section 232 tariffs on steel raised to 50%, materially lifting US benchmark HRC prices and spreads; North Star delivered underlying EBIT of $805.3M in FY2026 versus $267.2M in FY2025, operating at full post-expansion capacity

FY2025 results showed reported NPAT down sharply (down ~90% in headline terms) due to a $438.9M impairment against BlueScope Coated Products (BCP) goodwill/intangibles in North America, reflecting slower-than-expected integration and turnaround progress
Board considered and rejected unsolicited acquisition proposals during the year that it judged undervalued the company relative to its earnings trajectory and returns profile

Major growth projects progressed through peak capex and into ramp-up: New Zealand EAF produced first 'heat' (3 August 2026), Western Sydney MCL7 achieved 'metal on strip' (4 August 2026), and the Port Kembla No.6 Blast Furnace reline is targeting early CY2027 startup at ~$1.3bn final cost

guidance.management_commentary: New CEO Tania Archibald and Chair Jane McAloon characterised FY2026 as a 'defining year,' emphasising the shift from an investment phase (major projects nearing completion) to a returns-focused phase, with distribution targets raised to at least 75% of free cash flow. Management highlighted a 'mixed' operating environment for FY2027: continued strength in the US (tariff-supported), recovery underway in Australia, strong Southeast Asian momentum, but persistent Chinese overcapacity weighing on Asian spreads. Management noted the Board rejected unsolicited acquisition approaches during the year as undervaluing the company.

bull_case: North Star is firing on all cylinders at full capacity with historically wide US spreads supported by 50% Section 232 tariffs, and 1H FY2027 guidance implies continued sequential earnings growth

Major capital programs (6BF reline, MCL7, NZ EAF, North Star debottlenecking) are moving from peak capex into ramp-up, setting up a ~$500m targeted annual EBIT uplift by 2030 without proportionate further investment

Capital returns are ramping sharply - $3.00/share delivered in CY2026 with another $3.00/share planned for CY2027 - supported by a strengthening balance sheet, retained investment-grade ratings and a raised 75%-of-FCF distribution target

Diversified, multi-domestic portfolio (Australia, US, NZ, Asia) provides resilience: strength in one region (currently the US) can offset weakness elsewhere (currently China/Asia spreads and NZ transition costs)

BCP turnaround and Southeast Asian JV growth offer incremental upside from currently depressed or improving bases, and the Board's rejection of takeover approaches signals management's confidence the market is undervaluing the franchise
bear_case: Current earnings strength is heavily dependent on elevated US Section 232 tariffs; any future rollback, trade deal, or exemption would sharply compress North Star spreads and could reverse a large share of the FY2026 earnings improvement

Persistent Chinese steel overcapacity structurally caps Asian and Australian export spreads, and there is no clear catalyst for this to resolve, keeping ASP export sales and CPA/China margins under pressure

The business remains fundamentally a cyclical commodity manufacturer; FY2022's ~$2.2bn peak underlying EBIT versus FY2025's ~$738m trough shows how quickly conditions - and the share price - can reverse when spreads compress

Net debt has risen materially (from $28.4M to $600M in FY2026) as distributions were front-loaded relative to completion of major capex, reducing balance sheet flexibility if the cycle turns before projects are fully cash-generative

Execution risk remains on multiple fronts simultaneously: BCP turnaround, NZ EAF/6BF reline ramp-ups, and a new CEO in her first year, any of which could disappoint versus the ambitious 2030 EBIT growth targets
